item.title: Collaborative Intelligence in Operations Research: Models, Methods, and Applications
item.content:encoded:
Olga Battaïa, Kedge Business School

Yasser Dessouky, San Jose State University

Reza Zanjirani Farahani, Paris School of Business

Masood Fathi, University of Skövde

Madjid Tavana, La Salle University

Modern operations research requires approaches combining human expertise with artificial intelligence and distributed problem-solving. This special issue addresses how collaborative intelligence—the synergy between human decision-makers, AI systems, and mathematical models—can enhance adaptability and efficiency in complex operational environments.

Traditional OR methods struggle with dynamic and uncertain decision-making. While AI offers computational power, autonomous systems face challenges with uncertainty and interpretability. Collaborative intelligence bridges this gap by leveraging human intuition alongside AI capabilities.

The special issue welcomes theoretical and applied research on collaborative, multi-agent, and adaptive decision-making frameworks that advance how human-AI partnership, multi-agent coordination, and data-driven learning enhance operations research methodologies.

Appel publié par Annals of Operations Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Human-AI collaboration in OR models
  • AI output visualization and interpretability
  • Multi-agent optimization and game theory
  • Decentralized optimization algorithms
  • Adaptive OR frameworks
  • Online learning and adaptive control
  • Machine learning for OR applications
  • Learning-based optimization
  • Predictive analytics and simulation
  • Multi-agent coordination
  • Distributed problem-solving
  • Decision support systems
